submission-package/essay/symbolon/episte.body: --- title: "Hypostasis of the Archons — Bentley Layton online translation" source_id: hypostasis-archons-layton primary_domain: biblical-studies node_type: source-house record_type: primary-text-translation ownership: canonical-source-house schema_version: 1 author: - Anonymous translator: - Bentley Layton title_full: The Hypostasis of the Archons metadata_status: work-and-online-translator-identified edition_status: online-carrier-selected; print-impression-unidentified citation_status: citation-ready-for-online-translation quote_status: paraphrase-ready; no-exact-quotation source_relation: Paraphrased local_copy: working/sources-texts-references/primary-texts/nag-hammadi/hypostasis-archons-layton.html passage_surface: '#passages' --- # Hypostasis of the Archons — selected online translation The work is Nag Hammadi Codex II,4. The consulted [Early Christian Writings transcription](https://earlychristianwritings.com/text/archons.html) names Bentley Layton as translator and attributes the text to *The Nag Hammadi Library in English*, edited by James M. Robinson, via the Gnostic Society Library. Its footer does not identify a print impression. Cite this electronic carrier and the named episode; do not invent Coptic page-lines or printed page numbers. The complete translation, opening inquiry through closing hymn, was read on 8 September 2026. Its displayed lacunae remain unresolved. The local HTML SHA-256 is `46dd906dc6d6ac3ac362b2eb50cf65e6313cb15fd382d42f8a82794a99d8e66f`. This is a reading of the English carrier, not Coptic collation or verification of Barnstone–Meyer variants. The separate Stephen E. Robinson encyclopedia entry bears scholarly chronology, not primary translation authority. ## Passage sequence ### Formation **Paraphrase:** The rulers model Adam but cannot raise him; spirit arrives from beyond their jurisdiction. **Locator:** Opening apostolic inquiry through garden prohibition, in the linked online translation. **Verification:** complete episode read in complete telling; paraphrase-ready, 2026-09-08. **Consumer:** [whole, corresponding movement](submission-package/essay/symbolon/mytheme/worlds/late-antique-gnostic/hypostasis-archons-norea-sophia/WHOLE.md#25-adam-eve-and-the-rulers-attempt-to-possess-life). ### Woman, shadow and instruction **Paraphrase:** The spiritual woman escapes, leaving a violated shadow; the instructing principle enters and leaves the serpent. **Locator:** Sleep episode through expulsion and imposed toil, in the linked online translation. **Verification:** complete episode read in complete telling; paraphrase-ready, 2026-09-08. **Consumer:** [whole, corresponding movement](submission-package/essay/symbolon/mytheme/worlds/late-antique-gnostic/hypostasis-archons-norea-sophia/WHOLE.md#25-adam-eve-and-the-rulers-attempt-to-possess-life). ### Family and flood **Paraphrase:** Fratricide, Seth and Norea precede the flood; Norea burns the ark after exclusion. **Locator:** Cain and Abel through Noah rebuilding the ark, in the linked online translation. **Verification:** complete episode read in complete telling; paraphrase-ready, 2026-09-08. **Consumer:** [whole, corresponding movement](submission-package/essay/symbolon/mytheme/worlds/late-antique-gnostic/hypostasis-archons-norea-sophia/WHOLE.md#26-norea--flood--refusal-of-the-rulers). ### Norea and Eleleth **Paraphrase:** Norea refuses imposed descent; Eleleth rescues her and answers her inquiry. **Locator:** Rulers approaching Norea through her question about their origin, in the linked online translation. **Verification:** complete episode read in complete telling; paraphrase-ready, 2026-09-08. **Consumer:** [whole, corresponding movement](submission-package/essay/symbolon/mytheme/worlds/late-antique-gnostic/hypostasis-archons-norea-sophia/WHOLE.md#27-eleleth--rescue--revelation-of-the-root). ### Retrospective cosmology **Paraphrase:** Veil, shadow and matter precede the ruler; Zoe acts, Sabaoth changes allegiance, and envy generates death. **Locator:** Eleleth on Sophia through the completed pattern of the rulers, in the linked online translation. **Verification:** complete episode read in complete telling; paraphrase-ready, 2026-09-08. **Consumer:** [whole, corresponding movement](submission-package/essay/symbolon/mytheme/worlds/late-antique-gnostic/hypostasis-archons-norea-sophia/WHOLE.md#22-pistis-sophia--veil--shadow--matter--lower-ruler). ### Promised ending **Paraphrase:** Immediate rescue remains distinct from future disclosure, liberation and collective praise. **Locator:** Norea asking about her material origin through closing hymn, in the linked online translation. **Verification:** complete episode read in complete telling; paraphrase-ready, 2026-09-08. **Consumer:** [whole, corresponding movement](submission-package/essay/symbolon/mytheme/worlds/late-antique-gnostic/hypostasis-archons-norea-sophia/WHOLE.md#hypostasis-norea-root-return). ## Use and remaining control The telling **sources** the whole’s cosmology and disclosure sequence. --- title: Ephesians — SBL-hosted reverse-interlinear witness source_id: ephesians-sbl-reverse-interlinear primary_domain: biblical-studies node_type: source-house record_type: scriptural-text ownership: canonical-source-house schema_version: 1 author: - Pauline corpus title_full: The Letter of Paul to the Ephesians metadata_status: selected-witness-identified edition_status: local-scan-selected-text-checked citation_status: citation-ready-for-selected-witness-and-locator quote_status: paraphrase-ready; image-transcription-not-collated source_relation: Paraphrased local_copy: working/sources-texts-references/primary-texts/pauline-corpus/ephesians-sbl-reverse-interlinear/ephesians.pdf passage_surface: '#passages' --- # The Letter of Paul to the Ephesians The title identifies the letter as Paul’s; this source house does not settle historical authorship or date. The verified object is the 23-page Ephesians reverse-interlinear PDF hosted by SBLGNT, with Greek, English and grammatical rows. The selected passage is 1:9–10 on PDF page2, printed p.972. Full edition and translation metadata remain to be collated; the file is identified by URL and local hash. [Acquired witness](https://www.sblgnt.com/download/revint/70-Ephesians.pdf). Retrieved and selected text checked on 8 September 2026. Local SHA-256: `c8a46b30d2a7febb1608140360420b9d411f80033eb2567a64c6b5f2670c4651`. The witness **sources** [the historical branch](submission-package/essay/symbolon/episteme/etymologies/apportionment-and-economy/HISTORICAL-BRANCHES.md) and **qualifies** the historical comparison in its [whole-field](submission-package/essay/symbolon/episteme/etymologies/apportionment-and-economy/WHOLE-FIELD.md). Taylor’s generated operation remains distinct from the historical proposition. ## Selected passages ### q001 — Administration in the fullness of times **Paraphrase:** Disclosure of the divine purpose leads into an administration of the fullness of times and the gathering of things in heaven and on earth in Christ. The arrangement has an explicitly temporal and Christological office. This passage does not claim that every economy necessarily restores all of its participants in the same way. **Locator:** Ephesians 1:9–10; PDF page2, printed p.972. **Verification:** embedded text read and selected passage identified; no exact quotation or full-work collation claim.

--- title: "Laozi — Tao Teh King, translated by James Legge" source_id: laozi-legge-tao-teh-king primary_domain: chinese-philosophy node_type: source-house record_type: primary-text-translation ownership: canonical-source-house schema_version: 1 metadata_status: identified-online-carrier edition_status: selected-online-carrier-accessed-2026-09-08 citation_status: citation-ready-for-selected-carrier quote_status: paraphrase-ready; no-exact-quotation source_relation: Paraphrased local_copy: working/sources-texts-references/primary-texts/laozi/legge-gutenberg216.html passage_surface: '#passages' --- # Laozi — Tao Teh King, translated by James Legge The selected English carrier is Project Gutenberg ebook 216, *The Tao Teh King, or The Tao and Its Characteristics*, attributed to Lao-Tse and translated by James Legge. Its header records release 12 July 2008 and update 4 February 2013. The underlying print impression is not identified here. Cite this electronic translation and chapter; no modern Chinese critical edition or variant collation is claimed. [Selected electronic text](https://www.gutenberg.org/files/216/216-h/216-h.htm). Chapters 25, 28 and 32 were read completely on 8 September 2026; other chapters are not claimed as this reading scope. ## Chapter 25 **Paraphrase:** Tentative designation follows the unnamed. The four greats include the king; the sequence returns human law through earth and heaven to Tao's own character. **Locator:** 25.1–4. **Verification:** complete chapter read; paraphrase-ready. King/human variants require separate Chinese collation. ## Chapter 28 **Paraphrase:** Paired differences return to simplicity; material divided into vessels is placed beside governmental office and nonviolent rule. **Locator:** 28.1–2, including all three verse stanzas and closing prose. **Verification:** complete chapter read; paraphrase-ready. Legge's nonviolence does not certify the protected history's stronger non-severing gloss. ## Chapter 32 **Paraphrase:** Nameless simplicity passes into named action; rest limits error, and streams relate to rivers and seas. **Locator:** 32.1–5. **Verification:** complete chapter read; paraphrase-ready. Chang's reception, alternative translations and Chinese wording remain independently collatable; QL alignment belongs to Taylor. --- title: "Lewis and Short — A Latin Dictionary (1879)" source_id: lewis-short-1879-latin-dictionary primary_domain: classical-philology node_type: source-house record_type: dictionary ownership: canonical-source-house schema_version: 1 author: [Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short] title_full: A Latin Dictionary year: 1879 publisher: Clarendon Press metadata_status: identified edition_status: online-transcriptions-of-1879-work; print-not-collated citation_status: citation-ready-for-named-online-entries quote_status: selected-lexical-phrase-verified; no-ancient-passage-quotation source_relation: Paraphrased passage_surface: '#passages' --- # Lewis and Short — A Latin Dictionary ## Work and access Lewis, Charlton T., and Charles Short. *A Latin Dictionary*. Oxford: Clarendon Press, 1879. The selected witnesses are the Scaife ATLAS and Alatius transcriptions linked below, consulted on 8 September 2026. Cite the headword, sense and actual online witness. This record does not claim collation of the complete printed dictionary or independent reading of every ancient passage cited by its editors. Its nineteenth-century comparative reconstructions are not adopted as present specialist consensus. ## Use and return The dictionary **sources** Latin semantic distinctions in [E2 Arbitration](submission-package/essay/symbolon/episteme/etymologies/arbitration-hybris-regard-anamnesis/WHOLE-FIELD.md) and [E3 Fides–Credere](submission-package/essay/symbolon/episteme/etymologies/trust-place-logos-nomos-natio-credere/WHOLE-FIELD.md). Their generated relations remain authorial register 3. The lexical evidence supplies particular attested senses and a recoverable citation chain; it does not derive the QL field or establish an institutional chronology. ## Selected lexical witnesses ### q001 — Fides: reliance and credibility **Paraphrase:** the entry connects *fides* with *fido* and distinguishes reliance upon someone or something, credibility and fidelity. Its testimony example cites Cicero, *Pro Sulla* 3.10; the relation of competence and justice to confidence cites *De officiis* 2.9.33. **Locator and verification:** s.v. *fides*, initial literal senses and transferred quality; [Scaife entry n18127](https://atlas.perseus.tufts.edu/dictionaries/entry/urn:cite2:scaife-viewer:dictionary-entries.atlas_v1:lat.ls.perseus-eng2-n18127/), selected entry text read 2026-09-08. The stringed-instrument homograph is separate. No exact Ciceronian quotation is promoted. ### q002 — Credo: lending, protection and confidence **Paraphrase:** the entry distinguishes lending, committing something to another's protection, confidence and belief. It gives *creditum* as a loan and cites Cato, *De agri cultura* 5.4 in its discussion of lending under an owner's authority. **Locator and verification:** s.v. *credo*, business use and transferred uses; [Scaife entry n11525](https://atlas.perseus.tufts.edu/dictionaries/entry/urn:cite2:scaife-viewer:dictionary-entries.atlas_v1:lat.ls.perseus-eng2-n11525/), selected senses read 2026-09-08. Cato's primary passage and the proposed deeper reconstruction retain independent collation tasks. E3's before/after-arbitration relation is not the dictionary's chronology. ### q003 — Natio: birth, kinds and peoples **Paraphrase:** the entry associates *natio* with *nascor*. Its uses range from birth through group or kind to peoples; examples also concern animals and things. Its political vocabulary does not define the modern nation-state. **Locator and verification:** s.v. *natio*, introductory morphology and senses I–II/B; [Alatius transcription](https://www.alatius.com/ls/index.php?met=up&ord=natio), read 2026-09-08. Primary contexts and the later history of national institutions are separate evidence tasks. ### q004 — Arbitrari: observation, weighing, judgment and credited testimony **Paraphrase:** *arbitror* carries observation into mental examination and weighing, then distinguishes judicial decision, testimony and opinion. The dictionary's judicial subsection records the exact lexical construction **“fidem alicui arbitrari”**, citing Plautus, *Bacchides* 3.6.41, for credit accorded to someone. **Locator and verification:** s.v. *arbitror*, I, II.A and II.B; [Alatius transcription](https://www.alatius.com/ls/index.php?met=up&ord=arbitror), full entry read 2026-09-08. The quoted four-word construction is verified as dictionary wording. It is not presented as a continuous quotation from an independently collated Plautus edition. E2's witness→weighing→decision distinction and the E3 Fides bridge now have this exact lexical witness; the ancient dramatic context remains to be recovered independently. ### q005 — Arbiter: witness and deciding office **Paraphrase:** the entry distinguishes a person present to see or hear from an appointed deciding office. Judicial uses include inquiry and settlement, followed by general judging and governing uses. Its selected examples concern boundary disputes and the distribution of an estate; these keep the object of judgment identifiable. **Locator and verification:** s.v. *arbiter*, introduction, I and II.A–C; [Alatius transcription](https://www.alatius.com/ls/index.php?l=arbiter), full entry read 2026-09-08. The dictionary's proposed going/coming derivation and historical account of Roman procedural change remain the editors' claims, requiring independent specialist collation before stronger use. The semantic distinction supports E2 without making witnessing and judging identical offices. ### q006 — Ratio — reckoning and rendering an account **Paraphrase:** The entry connects ratio with reor/ratus and distinguishes reckoning, account, calculation and computation. Its examples include receipts and expenditure and rendering an account. This attests the selected Latin semantic field; it does not verify a common ancestry with Greek arithmos or harmony. **Locator and verification:** s.v. ratio, introduction and literal accounting senses; https://atlas.perseus.tufts.edu/dictionaries/entry/urn:cite2:scaife-viewer:dictionary-entries.atlas_v1:lat.ls.perseus-eng2-n40449/ ; selected senses read 2026-09-08, raw witness retained in T21-E6-private-development-packet.json. Paraphrase-ready to the online entry, with no independently verified ancient quotation or print collation. E6-ratio consumes this range while retaining A15’s native derivation and separate comparative-root debt. The entry **sources** [E6’s historical branch](submission-package/essay/symbolon/episteme/etymologies/apportionment-and-economy/HISTORICAL-BRANCHES.md) and its [whole-field](submission-package/essay/symbolon/episteme/etymologies/apportionment-and-economy/WHOLE-FIELD.md), with the institutional relation at register 3.

--- title: Liddell–Scott–Jones — A Greek-English Lexicon (9th ed., 1940) source_id: lsj-1940-greek-english-lexicon primary_domain: classical-philology node_type: source-house record_type: dictionary ownership: canonical-source-house schema_version: 1 author: - Henry George Liddell - Robert Scott - Henry Stuart Jones title_full: A Greek-English Lexicon year: 1940 edition: Ninth edition metadata_status: identified edition_status: selected-online-transcriptions; print-not-collated citation_status: citation-ready-for-named-online-entries quote_status: selected-senses-paraphrase-ready; no-exact-quotation source_relation: Paraphrased passage_surface: '#passages' --- # A Greek-English Lexicon Liddell, Henry George, and Robert Scott. *A Greek-English Lexicon*. Revised by Henry Stuart Jones with Roderick McKenzie. 9th ed. Oxford: Clarendon Press, 1940. Selected LSJ entry transcriptions were read at the Berlin-Brandenburg Academy’s CLD and Scaife ATLAS on 8 September 2026. Other dictionaries displayed on the same page retain separate authorship. Cite headword, sense and the actual transcription. Primary passages cited inside a lexicon are leads until independently collated. The source **sources** lexical distinctions in [E2 Arbitration](submission-package/essay/symbolon/episteme/etymologies/arbitration-hybris-regard-anamnesis/WHOLE-FIELD.md) and [E3 Fides–Credere](submission-package/essay/symbolon/episteme/etymologies/trust-place-logos-nomos-natio-credere/WHOLE-FIELD.md). Those fields’ generated operations remain authorial register 3. ## Selected lexical witnesses ### q001 — Topos **Paraphrase:** The entry distinguishes physical place, situated position, a passage in an author and a rhetorical topic. Aeschines 3.78 and Aristotle, Rhetoric 1358a14, are dictionary witnesses for distinct uses. These senses do not establish the authorial Arche-Topos compound or a mathematical theorem. **Locator:** s.v. τόπος, place/position, textual passage and rhetorical topic. **Access:** [selected LSJ transcription](https://cld.bbaw.de/lemma/grc/τόπος). **Verification:** named senses read 2026-09-08; no full-dictionary or independently collated ancient quotation claim. ### q002 — Logos **Paraphrase:** The entry distinguishes reckoning, monetary accounts, account-giving, esteem, relation and mathematical ratio. Euclid V, definition 3, is cited for ratio. Their shared headword does not collapse their objects; the selected semantic range does not establish a complete philosophy of Logos. **Locator:** s.v. λόγος, LSJ I.1–4 and II.1–2. **Access:** [selected LSJ transcription](https://cld.bbaw.de/lemma/grc/λόγος). **Verification:** named senses read 2026-09-08; no full-dictionary or independently collated ancient quotation claim. ### q003 — Nomos **Paraphrase:** The entry associates νόμος with νέμω and distinguishes customary usage from law or ordinance. The differently accented νομός has its own entry. This is lexical evidence, not proof of a compulsory pasture-to-state history or of the essay’s sixfold. **Locator:** s.v. νόμος, introduction and habitual practice/custom/law senses. **Access:** [selected LSJ transcription](https://atlas.perseus.tufts.edu/dictionaries/entry/urn:cite2:scaife-viewer:dictionaries.v1:lsj-n71005/). **Verification:** named senses read 2026-09-08; no full-dictionary or independently collated ancient quotation claim. ### q004 — Krisis **Paraphrase:** The entry derives the noun from κρίνω and distinguishes separating, judging, choosing and judicial proceedings. Its Aristotle Politics 1275a23 citation connects judgment and office within the cited civic context. The dictionary is the verified witness here; that Aristotelian passage has not been independently collated for this card. **Locator:** s.v. κρίσις, LSJ introductory and decision/judgment senses. **Access:** [selected LSJ transcription](https://cld.bbaw.de/lemma/grc/κρίσις). **Verification:** named senses read 2026-09-08; no full-dictionary or independently collated ancient quotation claim. ### q005 — Hybris **Paraphrase:** The initial sense concerns overbearing violence and insolence; the Odyssey suitors supply several cited examples. The semantic witness is narrower than Taylor’s exact theorem of a local determination occupying its determining condition. That theorem retains authorial standing; the lexicon does not independently derive it. **Locator:** s.v. ὕβρις, LSJ initial violence/insolence sense. **Access:** [selected LSJ transcription](https://cld.bbaw.de/lemma/grc/ὕβρις). **Verification:** named senses read 2026-09-08; no full-dictionary or independently collated ancient quotation claim. ### q006 — Anamnesis **Paraphrase:** The entry distinguishes calling to mind or recollection, reminders, a memorial sacrifice, and a separate lunar-return use. Its recollection citations include Plato, Phaedo 72e and 92d, Philebus 34c, and Aristotle, De memoria 451a21. These are dictionary witnesses; no complete Platonic argument is established by this card. **Locator:** s.v. ἀνάμνησις, introductory recollection sense and senses 2–3. **Access:** [selected LSJ transcription](https://atlas.perseus.tufts.edu/dictionaries/entry/urn:cite2:scaife-viewer:dictionaries.v1:lsj-n7019/). **Verification:** entry read 2026-09-08; selected senses paraphrase-ready, ancient citation contexts and print edition not independently collated. **Consumer:** E2 recollection branch; the authorial return remains register 3. ### q007 — Homologia **Paraphrase:** The entry distinguishes agreement and verbal consistency; assent, admission and concession; and compacts, including terms of peace or surrender. Plato, Symposium 187b and Theaetetus 164c, Aristotle, Topics 110a33, and the historical treaty citations are lexical witnesses here, not independently collated primary passages. The semantic range does not establish that every agreement is true, freely made or an instance of QL homology. **Locator:** s.v. ὁμολογία, agreement, admission and compact senses, including the peace/truce/surrender sub-sense. **Access:** [selected LSJ transcription](https://atlas.perseus.tufts.edu/dictionaries/entry/urn:cite2:scaife-viewer:dictionaries.v1:lsj-n73748/). **Verification:** named senses read 2026-09-08; no print-edition collation or exact quotation claim. **Consumer:** E5 historical Greek branch and homological-agreement office; evidence register 2, with the authorial comparison at register 3. ### q008 — Analogia **Paraphrase:** The entry distinguishes mathematical and general proportion, analogy including grammatical analogy, relation, and correspondence or resemblance. Aristotle, Nicomachean Ethics 1131a31, is a dictionary locator for the equality-of-ratios sense; Plato, Timaeus 31c–32c, is another cited witness. These primary passages were not independently collated. The range does not identify proportional analogy, focal predication and qualified predication as one historical doctrine. **Locator:** s.v. ἀναλογία, LSJ I–IV, including I.2 and II.2. **Access:** [selected LSJ transcription](https://atlas.perseus.tufts.edu/dictionaries/entry/urn:cite2:scaife-viewer:dictionaries.v1:lsj-n6926/). **Verification:** named senses read 2026-09-08 from the Scaife entry, retrieved via HTTP after the browsing tool's open error; no print-edition collation or exact quotation claim. **Consumer:** E5 analogy/Greek branches and C63's differentiated comparison grammars; evidence register 2, with the authorial coordination at register 3. The agreement and proportion entries **source** [E5’s Greek historical branch](submission-package/essay/symbolon/episteme/etymologies/homology-and-analogy/HISTORICAL-BRANCHES.md#e5-greek). The corresponding [whole-field](submission-package/essay/symbolon/episteme/etymologies/homology-and-analogy/WHOLE-FIELD.md) retains the project’s operational comparison at register 3. ### q009 — Νέμω — distribution and holding a portion **Paraphrase:** The entry distinguishes distributing portions, assigning honour or privilege, and middle-voice holding as one’s portion. Examples concern meat, property and land. These are attested semantic offices; the dictionary citations are not independently collated primary passages and do not establish a single chronology from pasture to state. **Locator and verification:** s.v. νέμω, distributive active and possessive middle senses; https://www.perseus.tufts.edu/hopper/text?doc=Perseus%3Atext%3A1999.04.0057%3Aentry%3Dne%2Fmw ; read 2026-09-08, raw witness retained in T21-E6-private-development-packet.json. Paraphrase-ready to the online entry; print not collated. E6 branch E6-names consumes register-2 distribution/possession distinctions; its institutional return is register 3.
